As a result, key elements linked to the objective became difficult to identify. Moving forward, greater clarity around the session objective and a more deliberate plan for managing realism will significantly improve the effectiveness of delivery.

deliveries.comment: Frame was done with good realistic game picture (11v11), however it was not clear to players the session objective - was it to switch play, was it the cross, or the finishing? deliveries.actionPlan:

2. Ensure you go into observation and process only when you have hit some coaching/teaching moments. Progressing towards active defending / opposed will reduce repetition and may reduce success further more if you have not influence behaviour sufficiently prior.

deliveries.comment:
Considering this was Freya’s first day in the environment and she was not initially expecting to deliver, overall she did well with the opportunity provided.

Moving forward, it is important to think more deeply about the actions and pictures needed to bring the session objective to life.
The progression also reduced the quality and quantity of repetitions. The change into the opposed practice did not fully support the session objective, so refining the progression design will be important. Potential alternatives could include adding an extra defender or allowing supporting players to join the action rather than progressing straight into a 2v2.
There is also an opportunity to increase the level of technical detail provided in interventions. Positive reinforcement on the runs was good, but the next step is to coach the detail of the pass and the specific movements required to get in behind effectively.

Action Plan
1. Refine the design and progressions to maintain realism, relevance, and repetition throughout the session
2. Consider player actions and positioning more carefully to create realistic pictures aligned to the topic
3. Add more technical detail in interventions, particularly around the quality and timing of passes and runs behind the defence
